name: Non-Linear Factor Models
title: Non-Linear Factor Models
answer: Non-linear factor models are quantitative return models in which the relationship between a stock's return and its underlying factors is not assumed to be a straight line. They extend the classical linear factor framework, where returns are modelled as a weighted sum of exposures, by allowing interactions, thresholds, curvature and regime dependence. In practice they are used to explain cross-sectional returns, build portfolios and attribute performance, and they sit alongside linear factor models rather than replacing them outright.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on standard quantitative research infrastructure: a point-in-time database of prices, fundamentals and factor exposures, plus a compute environment capable of fitting many models across a large universe. Because non-linear methods are data-hungry, the binding constraint is usually data quality and history length rather than raw compute. The site's own coverage of 117 listed AI-related instruments and 516 company pages illustrates the kind of universe and entity data such models are typically estimated on.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners start from a set of candidate factors, then let a non-linear model learn how exposures map to returns. Common choices include tree ensembles such as gradient boosted trees, kernel methods, splines and piecewise regressions, and neural networks, with cross-validation and out-of-sample testing used to guard against overfitting. The output is usually a fitted exposure-return surface or a set of conditional betas rather than a single coefficient per factor, and researchers spend most of their time on feature construction, regularisation and stability checks.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Non-linear factor models raise familiar model risk concerns in sharper form, because their flexibility makes overfitting and spurious pattern discovery easier and their behaviour harder to explain to a risk committee or allocator. Firms therefore keep documentation of factor definitions, data lineage and model versions, and they monitor live performance against the research backtest.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward models that combine non-linear flexibility with interpretability, so that a portfolio manager can see which factors and interactions are driving a position. Expect more use of regularised and constrained architectures, greater attention to regime shifts and non-stationarity, and tighter integration between factor research and execution. As alternative data and machine learning tooling mature, the practical question is less whether non-linear models can be fitted and more whether they can be trusted and maintained in production.
